text: Ritesh Batra (born 12 June 1979) is an Indian film director and screenwriter. His Hindi-language debut feature film, The Lunchbox, premiered at the 2013 Cannes Film Festival and won the Rail d’Or (Grand Golden Rail). Batra also won the Toronto Film Critics Association Award for Best First Feature Film in 2014. The Lunchbox was the highest-grossing foreign film in North America, Europe, and Australia for 2014, grossing over US$25 Million, and was nominated for a BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language in 2015. He directed the English-language film The Sense of an Ending (2017), an adaptation of Julian Barnes’ Booker Prize-winning novel, and in 2017 released Our Souls at Night on Netflix. His latest film is Photograph, released in 2019. Ritesh grew up in a middle-class family in Mumbai, India; his father, Joginder Batra, worked in the Merchant Navy of India, and his mother, Manju Kapoor Batra, is a housewife. His elder sister, Radhika Batra Shah, runs a tea business. He completed his high school at AVM High School in Mumbai and later studied in the United States. After graduating from Drake University, Iowa, in Economics, he worked as a consultant at Deloitte for three years before returning to school to pursue filmmaking. He attended New York University but dropped out of the film school. Batra began his filmmaking career by writing and directing shorts. His Arab language short, Café Regular, Cairo, screened at over 40 international film festivals and won over 12 awards, including Critics Prize (FIPRESCI) Best Film at International Short Film Festival Oberhausen and Best Film at German Star of India. In 2009, he was part of the Sundance Screenwriters and Directors lab with his project "Story of Ram." He was later made the Time Warner Story Telling Fellow at Sundance Film Festival and Annenberg Fellow at Sundance Film Academy. In 2011, Batra returned to India to make a documentary on the lunchbox delivery system in Mumbai, which inspired his first feature film, The Lunchbox (2013). He developed this project through the TorinoFilmLab Framework programme in 2012. The Lunchbox premiered at the Cannes Critics Week 2013 and won the Rail d’Or (Grand Golden Rail). At Cannes, the movie sparked a bidding war, with Sony Pictures Classic acquiring the North American rights. The film has been nominated for 33 Awards and has won 25 so far. In 2014, Batra founded his own production company, PoeticLicense Motion Pictures, and is currently developing a slate of films. Short film: Café Regular Cairo (2011). Feature film: The Lunchbox (2013).
